description: Hi! We are Project NOAH - Navigation, Orbit, Astronomy, Horizon from The Winchester School - Jebel Ali! We are participating in the NASA Hackathon to create an exciting Space Mission Design Game. We welcome individuals passionate about mathematics, science, astronomy, coding, and technology. If you love exploring space solving problems and sharing creative ideas we would love to have you on our team. Together let's innovate and reach beyond the stars!
summary:
I developed AeroNOAH, an immersive space mission design game built for the NASA Space Mission Design challenge. I designed an interactive experience where players can conceptualize, build, and test custom spacecraft using real aerospace principles, navigate dynamic multi-stage rocket physics, and conduct surface exploration on 20 unique celestial bodies.

I built this project to address the NASA Hackathon challenge by turning complex orbital mechanics and mission planning into an engaging, hands-on simulation. It empowers users to understand the critical engineering trade-offs required in aerospace design—from managing mass ratios and thrust-to-weight ratios to executing surface engineering tasks.

I believe this project is important because it makes space exploration accessible and educational. By letting players visualize flight telemetry and solve engineering problems firsthand, I created a tool that sparks curiosity and inspires the next generation of space pioneers.
details:
AeroNOAH was developed with the goal of helping people understand the importance of effective budgeting, rocket formation, and the fundamentals of aerospace engineering through interactive, engaging, and hands-on activities. The project aims to make complex scientific and engineering concepts easier to understand by turning them into an enjoyable and educational gaming experience. Using real NASA data, I was able to design and create a game that combines real-world information with interactive challenges, allowing players to learn while having fun.

Through AeroNOAH, users can explore the different aspects of rocket development, understand the importance of managing resources and budgets, and gain a better appreciation of the planning and knowledge required in space exploration.

I hope that AeroNOAH will encourage curiosity, develop problem-solving skills, and inspire the next generation of astronauts, scientists, and engineers to explore the endless possibilities of space.

How does it work? - My objective is to make aerospace-related topics more accessible and interesting, especially for students and individuals who aspire to pursue careers in fields such as astronomy, aerospace engineering, and space exploration.

What Benefits does it have? - My project contains 15 question quiz designed to test your knowledge of astronomy. It also contains a mini-VAB (Vehicle Assembly Building) that has 40 rocket parts of different areas, fictional currency, some adjustments like capacity of astronauts, transportation system and structural material. After completing launch and reaching your given destination, you will have an option to explore your surroundings, a lot of hands-on activities, and a chance to make an impact that may change the world as we know it today.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? - I used HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

How is your project creative? - What makes my project unique is its use of real NASA data to create an educational game that connects real-world space exploration with hands-on learning. It combines science, technology, creativity, and problem-solving in a way that makes learning more engaging and accessible.

 What factors did I consider? - When creating AeroNOAH, I considered several important factors to make the project both fun and educational. First, I focused on accuracy by using real NASA data to provide reliable information. I also considered user engagement by making the game interactive and enjoyable.

Another factor was simplicity, as I wanted people with little knowledge of rockets and space to understand the concepts easily. I also focused on educational value, teaching users about budgeting, rocket formation, and resource management. I also had to write over 1,100 lines of code to make my ideas, project, and hard work come to life.

Lastly, I wanted the project to encourage creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving while inspiring people to learn more about space exploration and aerospace engineering.
